claims.text: Empirical content analysis of 243 ChatGPT distorted information samples identified 8 first-level error types in AIGC.

The 8 first-level error types of distorted information in AIGC are Overfitting, Logic errors, Reasoning errors, Mathematical errors, Unfounded fabrication, Factual errors, Text output errors, and Other errors.
The classification framework subdivides the 8 first-level error types into 31 second-level error types.
Inter-coder consistency using Holsti's method reached 89% in the second round of pre-coding across three coders.
Content analysis of the collected distorted information samples yielded 284 analysis units of error points.
The study establishes an empirical multi-stage content analysis method for categorizing AIGC distorted information based on pre-coding and test coding phases.

evidence.description: Utilizing ChatGPT as a case study, we conducted empirical content analysis on 243 instances of distorted information collected... The findings identified 8 first-level error types.

The findings identified 8 first-level error types: 'Overfitting'; 'Logic errors'; 'Reasoning errors'; 'Mathematical errors'; 'Unfounded fabrication'; 'Factual errors'; 'Text output errors'; and 'Other errors'.
The 8 first-level error types are further subdivided into 31 second-level error types.
Ultimately, the consistency among the three coders increased to 89%, meeting the anticipated reliability criteria and concluding the pre-coding process.
From the ChatGPT distorted information samples collected, 284 analysis units were extracted across the pre-coding and test coding phases.
The coding process comprised two key phases: pre-coding on 70% of samples (202 analysis units) and test coding on 30% of samples (82 analysis units) using three independent coders.

methodologies.name: Empirical Content Analysis with Multi-stage Coding Scheme Refinement
methodologies.description: A seven-step quantitative content analysis methodology using individual error points as analysis units, combining literature-derived taxonomies, pre-coding on 70% of samples, and test coding on 30% of samples by three independent coders to build an AIGC error taxonomy.
conditions: 243 conversation samples (218 GPT-3.5, 25 GPT-4) collected between Jan 1, 2023 and Dec 31, 2023
Three independent coders with standardized training and analysis memos
Inter-coder reliability evaluated using Holsti's method

limitations.text: The distortion samples were exclusively generated from ChatGPT, meaning the category list may lack comprehensiveness across other AIGC tools.
The sample collected from Typeform.com does not include all cases of distortion, which may cause some error categories to be missing.
The study solely encompasses error types specific to early versions of ChatGPT, which may become outdated as model performance improves.
The study exclusively focuses on text-based AIGC tools, overlooking image, audio, video, and multi-modal AIGC tools.
The inclusion of 'Discrimination' as a distorted information category involves subjective ideological considerations and remains controversial.
Prior studies and websites classification efforts rely solely on distorted samples without rigorous scientific frameworks or standardized criteria.

future_work.text: Select a broader range of samples from various other artificial intelligence generation tools and gather distortion data from multiple sources.
Monitor and track ongoing technological improvements in LLMs to update and refine the distorted information category list.
Broaden the scope of research to investigate distorted information in image, audio, video, and multi-modal AIGC tools.
Explore additional perspectives on whether it is reasonable to categorize 'Discrimination' under AIGC distorted information.
